messages:
maria: Running a 10k qps synthetic replay against the new kernel-selection branch. Saw a ~2.5x p95 regression compared to baseline when clients use short-lived connections.
de
vin: short-lived connections = new process per request or disabled keepalive?

maria: Verified both. Two modes: a) curl-style single request sockets, b) many tiny HTTP/1.1 connections with no pooling. Both show same tail. When I flip clients to keepalive + pool size 100, tail disappears.

hao: Did you repro with gRPC clients? That should use HTTP/2 multiplexing so pooling less relevant.

maria: Good call. With grpcurl-based replay p95 is close to baseline but p99 still spikes intermittently. Logs point to kernel selection path hitting slower AVX fallback on some sequences.

bench-bot: last-run summary: baseline p95=110ms p99=300ms; kernel-branch p95=270ms p99=820ms; qps=10k; concurrency simulated = 400.

sam: Two different issues smell here: client-side connection churn + TCP/TLS Nagle/handshake costs, and server path non-determinism causing occasional slow kernels under certain seq lengths. We should separate variables.

devin: Proposal: run three apples-to-apples runs with identical request traces: 1) synthetic steady concurrent HTTP/1.1 with persistent keepalives pools, 2) same trace but one-request sockets, 3) grpc multiplexed (HTTP/2) + single channel per client. Measure p50/p95/p99 and kernel selection traces.

hao: Also capture system-level metrics and perf samples around slow tokens. Add `perf record -F 99 -g` capture for the slow tail buckets and compare callgraphs.

maria: Did a quick check: when clients tear down TCP a lot, we see many TLS handshakes and kernel-selection decisions that pick non-AVX kernels as sequence length estimates are off (we lose accurate seq-length distribution from prefix caching due to fragmented requests).

sam: That makes sense — KV cache hit patterns change if requests arrive in tiny bursts and we re-warm caches per connection. Batching heuristics kick in differently.

devin: For the apples-to-apples, make sure TLS session resumption is toggled consistently. Some client libs do session resumption by default which hides the handshake cost. Use explicit flags to enable/disable. Example: curl `--no-sessionid` vs `--sessionid` for openssl builds.

maria: Re-ran with explicit TLS resumption disabled and pooled keepalives disabled. p95 jumped massively, p99 got catastrophic. With pooling+resumption p95 back to normal.

ops-bot: deploy noted: test cluster `load-harness-3` still on kernel-branch; CPU: a100x2, 64g memory.

hao: Action items: 1) bench infra: add replay harness mode that preserves client connection behavior from production traces (not just request timestamps). 2) Runtime: add debug logging for kernel-selection decision + batch size chosen per request. 3) Devex: add a checklist for 'apples-to-apples' that always specifies keepalive, pool size, TLS resumption, and grpc channel count.

sam: Also add a small synthetic that intentionally toggles short-lived vs keepalive in the same run so we can observe how KV cache and batching adapt over ramps.

maria: One more gotcha we found: Node/http clients default to Nagle enabled which interacts poorly with tiny request bodies and TLS; turning TCP_NODELAY on reduced one-way latency variance.

devin: Rough checklist for future load tests (copyable):
```
- use replay harness preserving connection lifetimes
- run HTTP/1.1 pooled, HTTP/1.1 churn, and HTTP/2 grpc modes
- fix TLS session resumption state explicitly
- set TCP_NODELAY consistently
- instrument kernel-selection logs + perf capture for slow tails
- compare with identical model weights and quantization profiles
```

maria: I'll turn this into a short doc and add a couple of sample harness configs in the repo. For now: if you run perf on the kernel-branch, make sure your client harness replicates production connection reuse.

hao: Thanks — saved a ton of time.

sam: :thumbsup:

bench-bot: archival: uploaded perf.tar.gz and harness traces to s3://redwood-load-tests/1767212345/
